t:
(a) Section 2002(a)(1) of the Social Security Act is amended by inserting “100 per centum of the expenditures during that quarter (which are not in excess of 2 per centum of the limitation applicable to that State under paragraph (2)(A) for the fiscal year in which such quarter occurs) for grants to qualified providers under section 2007,” after “an amount equal to”. 
    (b) Title XX of such Act is amended by redesignating section 2007 as section 2008 and inserting after section 2006 the following new section:


“child day care services
“Sec. 2007. (a) Subject to subsection (b), sums granted by a State to a qualified provider of child day care services (as defined in subsection (c)) to assist such provider in meeting its work incentive program expenses (as defined in subsection (c)) with respect to individuals employed in jobs related to the provision of child day care services in one or more child day care facilities of such provider, shall be deemed for purposes of section 2002 to constitute expenditures made by the State in accordance with the provisions of this title for the provision of child day care services.
“(b) The provisions of subsection (a) shall not be applicable with respect to any grant made to a particular qualified provider of child day care services to the extent that (as determined by the Secretary) such grant is or will be used to pay wages to any employee at an annual rate in excess of $6,000, in the case of a public or nonprofit private provider, or at an annual rate in excess of $5,000, or to pay more than 80 per centum of the wages of any employee, in the case of any other provider.
“(c) For purposes of this subsection—

“(1) 
the term ‘qualified provider of child day care services’, when used in reference to a recipient of a grant by a State, includes a provider of such services only if, of the total number of children receiving such services from such provider in the facility with respect to which the grant is made, at least 20 per centum thereof have some or all of the costs for the child day care services so furnished to them by such provider paid for under the State’s services program conducted pursuant to this title; and


“(2) 
the term ‘work incentive program expenses’ means expenses of a qualified provider of child day care services which constitute work incentive program expenses as defined in section 50B(a)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, or which would constitute work incentive program expenses as so defined if the provider were a taxpayer entitled to a credit (with respect to the wages involved) under section 40 of such Code.”. 
 
    (c) Sections 2002(a)(4)(C), 2002(a)(4)(D), and 2002(a)(5)(A) of such Act are each amended by striking out “2007(1)” and inserting in lieu thereof “2008(1)”. 
    (d) The amendments made by this section shall become effective on the date of the enactment of this Act, and shall apply with respect to grants made to qualified providers of child day care services during the period beginning October 1, 1979, and ending March 31, 1980.

fable.w: The section amends Title XX of the Social Security Act so that State grants to qualified child day care providers count as reimbursable expenditures, subject to wage caps and definitions. The tempting reading is that the involvement of States and private providers amounts to participation, but they are only grant makers and recipients in a funding scheme, which the definition excludes. The only federal decision is a unilateral determination by the Secretary, with no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: (as determined by the Secretary) such grant is or will be used to pay wages to any employee at an annual rate in excess of $6,000

qwen_block.w: This section defines how certain state grants to child care providers are treated for federal reimbursement purposes under the Social Security Act. It does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or create advisory bodies with non-federal members. The interaction described is a financial accounting mechanism for state expenditures, not a participatory decision-making process involving the public or outside entities in federal policy formulation.
qwen_block.s: sums granted by a State to a qualified provider of child day care services... shall be deemed for purposes of section 2002 to constitute expenditures made by the State

opus.w: This section sets federal matching rules and eligibility conditions for State grants to child day care providers. Grants and benefits are excluded from the definition of participation. The only federal decision is a determination the Secretary makes alone, with no required consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue for outside parties. Outside providers appear only as grant recipients, not as participants in a federal decision.
opus.s: to the extent that (as determined by the Secretary) such grant is or will be used to pay wages to any employee at an annual rate in excess of $6,000
opus.b: 1. **Analysis.** The tempting reading is that this is participation because outside parties appear: States give grants to private and nonprofit child day care providers, and the Secretary makes a determination about how grants are used. That reading fails. These are funding and eligibility rules for grants, which the definition excludes. The Secretary's decision about wages ("as determined by the Secretary") involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or rulemaking with anyone outside the federal government. Nothing gives an outside party a right to sue or object.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines how state grants to child care providers are counted as expenditures for federal matching purposes. It does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties before making a decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants from being considered participation. The Secretary's role is limited to verifying wage thresholds, which is an administrative check, not a participatory consultation.
qwen_chat.s: sums granted by a State to a qualified provider of child day care services... shall be deemed for purposes of section 2002 to constitute expenditures made by the State
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section involves "grants to qualified providers," it constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" are not participation. Furthermore, the text describes the mechanics of how state expenditures are calculated for federal matching purposes and defines terms for grant eligibility; it does not describe a process where outside parties consult with the federal government before a decision is made. The Secretary's role is limited to determining if a grant exceeds certain wage thresholds, which is an administrative enforcement action, not a participatory decision-making process involving outside consultation.
